episode.title: Route Ctrl+W to the text buffer's existing previous-word deletion operation
episode.before: At parent commit 27a773d5b29ce361ea3116578dd3de462030b696, the text buffer already implemented deleteWordLeft and already routed modified Backspace/Delete-character input to that operation, but handleInput had no branch for the normalized event combination key.ctrl=true with input='w'. InputPrompt forwarded otherwise-unhandled input events to buffer.handleInput, so Ctrl+W reached the dispatcher without invoking previous-word deletion.
episode.after: At commit 98dcf43214da5f03055213f02f999b047a5f00d4, handleInput recognizes key.ctrl=true with input='w' and invokes the existing deleteWordLeft operation. That operation removes the preceding word and adjacent non-word characters according to the buffer's established logic, updates the cursor, clears the preferred column, and participates in undo handling. Existing modified-Backspace and other key mappings remain in their prior order and are unchanged.
episode.diff: One conditional branch was inserted in packages/cli/src/ui/components/shared/text-buffer.ts immediately after end-of-line mappings and before modified-Backspace handling: else if (key['ctrl'] && input === 'w') deleteWordLeft();. No deletion algorithm, call site, interface, or test file changed.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 98dcf43214da5f03055213f02f999b047a5f00d4 has parent 27a773d5b29ce361ea3116578dd3de462030b696 and is titled "Add a keybinding for ctrl+w to delete the previous word. (#582)".
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller 98dcf43214da5f03055213f02f999b047a5f00d4; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: The entire implementation diff is one added handleInput branch that matches key.ctrl with input 'w' and calls deleteWordLeft; only text-buffer.ts changed.
In the parent state, handleInput mapped movement, home/end, modified Backspace, modified Delete, ordinary Backspace, and Ctrl+D, but contained no Ctrl+W branch.

The reused deleteWordLeft operation already handled start-of-buffer and line-boundary cases, recorded undo state, scanned left across non-word and word characters, removed the selected span, moved the cursor to the deletion start, and cleared the preferred column.

The new Ctrl+W branch is part of the dispatcher's mutually exclusive else-if chain, positioned after Ctrl+E and before modified-Backspace word deletion, leaving subsequent character-deletion and printable-input branches unchanged.

InputPrompt creates the shared text buffer and forwards input events not consumed by submit or arrow-history handling to buffer.handleInput(input, key), making the new mapping reachable from the interactive prompt.

The existing text-buffer unit suite exercises handleInput for printable characters, Enter, Backspace, arrows, pasted ANSI text, and terminal newline representation, establishing handleInput as the unit-test boundary for key dispatch.

No test was added by the commit, and the existing test file explicitly lists deleteWordLeft and deleteWordRight among operations needing more tests; therefore the checkout contains no direct regression oracle for Ctrl+W.
The CLI package defines `vitest run` as its test command, but the pinned change provides no recorded status-check metadata and no direct Ctrl+W test result.

candidate_atomics.name: route_normalized_shortcut_to_existing_edit_action
candidate_atomics.title: Route a normalized shortcut to an existing semantic edit action
candidate_atomics.description: Add a narrowly matched modifier-plus-input branch at the shared input-dispatch boundary and delegate to the buffer's established previous-word deletion operation, preserving the existing edit semantics and neighboring shortcut mappings.

semantic_action.intent: Make a terminal control chord perform the same previous-word deletion behavior already available through other normalized key events.
semantic_action.module_role: Shared text-input event dispatcher backed by semantic buffer-edit operations
semantic_action.pre_state: The input dispatcher receives normalized modifier and input fields and an appropriate semantic deletion operation already exists, but the requested chord has no dispatch branch.
semantic_action.post_state: When the dispatcher receives the exact requested control chord, it invokes the existing previous-word deletion operation without changing that operation or unrelated shortcut behavior.
semantic_action.validation: At the handleInput boundary, initialize text containing a preceding word, place the cursor after it, dispatch input='w' with ctrl=true, and assert the same text and cursor result as deleteWordLeft; also rerun existing handleInput tests to detect routing regressions. This targeted oracle is prescribed by the implementation boundary but was not added or recorded in the pinned change.

candidate_workflows.name: add_conflict_aware_shortcut_by_reusing_semantic_editing
candidate_workflows.title: Add a shortcut by reusing an existing semantic editing operation
candidate_workflows.description: Extend a normalized key-event dispatcher with an exact shortcut match that delegates to an established editing primitive, retain the dispatch chain's existing precedence, and validate both the new route and neighboring routes.

workflow_graph.goal: Expose an existing buffer-edit capability through an additional normalized keyboard chord without duplicating editing logic or changing unrelated input behavior.
when_to_use: A shared input dispatcher already receives normalized character and modifier fields.
The requested shortcut should invoke an existing, independently defined semantic edit operation.
The chord is currently unhandled at the dispatcher reached by the interactive input call site.
anti_goals: Do not reimplement word-boundary deletion inside the key-event branch.
Do not globally reinterpret the input character when the required modifier is absent.
Do not reorder or broaden unrelated shortcut predicates merely to add the new chord.
Do not claim regression coverage when no direct shortcut test has been added or run.
not_applicable_when: The terminal or UI layer does not deliver the chord as the expected normalized modifier-plus-input combination.
The requested behavior has no existing semantic operation and therefore requires a separately specified editing implementation.
An earlier call-site handler consumes the event before it reaches the shared dispatcher.
The proposed chord conflicts with a higher-priority application command that must retain ownership.
inputs: Normalized event representation for the desired chord
Existing semantic edit operation and its state behavior
Dispatcher ordering and surrounding shortcut predicates
Interactive call site forwarding events to the dispatcher
Unit-test boundary and runnable package test command
workflow_graph.entry_state: The semantic previous-word deletion operation exists and is reachable through some input forms, while the requested control chord reaches the shared dispatcher but has no exact mapping.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The exact normalized chord delegates to the existing semantic edit operation at the shared dispatch boundary; unrelated mappings and the editing algorithm remain unchanged, and any missing direct regression test is explicitly recorded.

steps.condition: Use only after confirming the chord reaches this dispatcher, is not already handled, and the target semantic operation already implements the desired edit.
steps.validation: Inspect the ordered predicate to confirm it matches only ctrl=true with input='w', delegates to deleteWordLeft, and leaves adjacent mappings unchanged; then exercise handleInput with the chord and compare its resulting text and cursor to direct deleteWordLeft behavior.

validation_ladder: Static diff check: only the exact shortcut predicate and delegation are added at the dispatcher boundary.
Call-site check: interactive input not consumed by submit or history navigation falls through to the shared dispatcher.
Behavioral unit check: dispatch the new chord against representative text and assert text, cursor, and handled-state changes consistent with the existing semantic operation.
Regression check: run the CLI package's existing Vitest suite, especially handleInput tests.
Gap disclosure: if the targeted shortcut test is absent or not executed, retain validation as incomplete rather than inferring success from the one-line diff.
stop_conditions: Stop if the normalized event shape for the chord cannot be established.
Stop if another handler consumes the chord before the dispatcher.
Stop if the target semantic operation does not match the requested behavior.
Stop or redesign if the new predicate overlaps a higher-priority shortcut.
Do not mark validation complete without a direct behavioral oracle or recorded execution result.
unresolved_or_deferred: The pinned commit added no direct Ctrl+W regression test.
PR reviews and status-check results are unavailable in the evidence bundle.

unresolved_questions: Was Ctrl+W manually or automatically verified on every supported terminal/input backend? The available checkout and GitHub bundle do not provide that evidence.
Why was no direct handleInput regression test added for the new mapping despite the test file identifying word-deletion coverage as incomplete?
